title: Mapping the Failure of Sparse Feature Representations Under Distributional Shift: SAEs Trained on Web Text Applied to Code

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if SAE tools do not transfer to code/scientific domains, safety interpretability for code models and specialized applications requires domain-specific tooling, a major practical obstacle.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses pre-trained SAEs, just computes activation statistics on different datasets. Loading data from The Stack/PubMed and comparing feature statistics is accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: compute 3 metrics (L0 sparsity, feature overlap, coherence check) on 2 OOD datasets vs. in-distribution baseline. Clear and bounded.

novelty.reasoning: SAE generalization under distributional shift has been studied (arXiv 2502.19964) and transferability results show inconsistent performance (EMNLP 2025). The geometry of concepts paper documents domain-specific feature activation patterns. The specific framing of web-text SAEs applied to code/scientific text is partially novel, but the broader OOD concern is well-established.

evidence.source: SAE Features for Classifications and Transferability (EMNLP 2025)
evidence.finding: Studies SAE feature transferability across tasks and datasets, finding inconsistent transfer ability with high variance out of distribution.
Directly studies SAE generalization to out-of-distribution inputs, finding residual stream probes show high variance OOD.

evidence.source: The Geometry of Concepts: SAE Feature Structure (2025)
evidence.finding: Documents that different lobes of SAE feature space activate on different document types, with distinct clusters for code/math vs. scientific text.
